s1.syndrome_frame: A firm, enlarged nasal ala with a recurrent lesion in the nasal vestibule mucosa
salient_findings: Recurrent lesion in the nasal vestibule mucosa
Tumor within the nasal vestibule floor and ala
key_facts: The patient is a woman in her 50s
The patient is a never-smoker
The lesion was first noticed 5 years prior to presentation
The initial biopsy reported a solid and cystic hidradenoma
The lesion recurred 8 months prior to presentation
The lesion was excised but recurred quickly after 2 months
Pathology showed p63 positive and p16 negative results
Imaging showed a thicker right ala compared to the left ala
Tumor was found in the ala and its extension into the floor of the nasal vestibule

shortlist.label: adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: recurrent lesion with positive margins and atypical keratinocytes

shortlist.label: squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: p63 positive and p16 negative results, consistent with squamous cell origin

shortlist.label: hidradenoma
shortlist.why_kept: initial biopsy reported solid and cystic hidradenoma, although recurrence suggests possible malignant transformation

shortlist.label: lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: although less likely, lymphoma can present with nasal masses and should be considered in the differential

shortlist.label: sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: given the rapid recurrence and aggressive behavior of the lesion, sarcoma is a plausible consideration

raw.rationale: The initial biopsy reported a solid and cystic hidradenoma, and the pathology results showed p63 positive and p16 negative, which are consistent with hidradenoma.

rejected.label: adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: No specific evidence of glandular differentiation

rejected.label: squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: p16 negative and lack of clear squamous differentiation

rejected.label: lymphoma
rejected.why: No evidence of lymphoid cells or lymphoma-specific markers
